info.title: IT Glue API
info.description:
Unofficial, best-effort OpenAPI specification generated from the official IT Glue developer documentation. It is not published or endorsed by IT Glue or Kaseya.

- Documentation: https://api.itglue.com/developer/
- Pagination: https://help.itglue.kaseya.com/help/Content/1-admin/it-glue-api/pagination-in-the-it-glue-api.html
- Sorting and filtering: https://help.itglue.kaseya.com/help/Content/1-admin/it-glue-api/sorting-and-filtering-in-the-it-glue-api.html
- Generator and change history: https://github.com/Celerium/ITGlue-OpenAPI

Requests authenticate with the `x-api-key` header. Payloads use `Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json`.

The version of this document follows the IT Glue product version (see the release notes). When the API changes without a product version change, the current date (`YYYYMMDD`) is appended.

tags.name: Attachments
tags.description:
An attachment refers to a file upload associated with an asset.

This resource allows you to manage all attachments in your account. Note that attachments are accessed from the relevant endpoints (GET /configurations, GET /passwords, etc.) using the `include=attachments` parameter to return the file attachments in the relationships attributes of the requested objects. Example: /configurations/1?include=attachments

An attachment can belong to only one asset. Each asset can have relationships with one or more attachments.

tags.name: Checklists
tags.description:
Checklist

This resource allows you to manage checklists on your account.

tags.name: Configuration Interfaces
tags.description:
A configuration interface refers to an IP address for a networked device.

This resource allows you to manage all IP and MAC addresses associated with the configurations in your account. Configuration interface IDs can be used to POST new configurations.

A configuration interface can belong to only one configuration and can have only one IP address and one MAC address. Each configuration can have relationships with one or more configuration interfaces, one of which will be a primary interface.

Note that when a configuration is created or updated with a new primary IP or MAC address, this creates or updates the configuration Interface object. If the primary IP or MAC address in the configuration interface object is updated, this also updates the primary IP or MAC address on the configuration.

tags.name: Configuration Statuses
tags.description:
A configuration status refers to the status that can be maintained on a configuration, for example, active or inactive.

This resource is used to manage information about configuration statuses for your account. Configuration status IDs can be used to POST new configurations.

A configuration status may be referenced by one ore more configurations. Each configuration can have one configuration status, but it's not required.

tags.name: Configuration Types
tags.description:
A configuration type refers to the type categorization of a configuration, usually a type of device.

This resource is used to manage information about configuration types for your account. Configuration type IDs can be used to POST new configurations.

A configuration type may be referenced by one or more configurations. It's required that each configuration item have one configuration type.

tags.name: Configurations
tags.description:
A configuration refers to a device you manage for a client organization.

The Configurations resource allows you to manage information about all configurations in your account.

A configuration can belong to only one organization. Each configuration can have a primary IP address, a primary MAC address, plus one or more additional IP and MAC addresses that are maintained in a separate Configuration Interfaces resource.

tags.name: Contact Types
tags.description:
A contact type refers to the type categorization of a contact, for example, an approver or an owner.

This resource is used to manage information about contact types for your account. Contact type IDs can be used to POST new contacts.

A contact type may be referenced by one or more contacts. Each contact can have one contact type, but it's not required.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description:
A contact refers to a contact in a client organization.

The Contacts resource allows you to manage information about all contacts in your account.

A contact can belong to only one organization. Each contact can have one location, which is maintained as a separate Locations resource.

tags.name: Countries
tags.description:
A country refers to any distinct national entity.

The Countries resource allows you to retrieve information about the country names that IT Glue supports. Country IDs can be used to POST new locations.

Supported countries may be referenced by one or more locations. Each location can have one country, but it's not required.

tags.name: Document Images
tags.description: A Document Image represents an uploaded image file associated with a Document Document Images can be used in two contexts: - Gallery Images - Associated with a Document::Gallery or Document::Step section - Inline Images - Embedded directly in Document content without a gallery Images are uploaded as Base64-encoded data and stored with multiple size variants: - original-src: Full resolution original image URL (for display in galleries) - slim-src: Medium-sized variant URL (optimized for web viewing) - thumbnail-src: Small thumbnail variant URL (for previews) - inline-resource-url: Relative path format for embedding images in section content. Used when CREATING or UPDATING section content with inline images. Returns null for gallery images. Format: /org_id/docs/doc_id/developer/images/image_id CREATING SECTIONS WITH INLINE IMAGES: - First create an inline image with target: { type: 'document', id: } - From the response, copy the inline-resource-url value (e.g., /1065811/docs/2288222/developer/images/794078) - Create or update a section with content containing: - DO NOT use S3 URLs (original-src) in content - the system needs to parse the relative path - The system will automatically convert relative paths to S3 URLs in rendered-content TARGET ATTRIBUTE: All images include a 'target' attribute that identifies the image placement: - { type: 'gallery', id: } for gallery-associated images (inline-resource-url will be null) - { type: 'document', id: } for inline images (inline-resource-url will be the relative path)

tags.name: Document Sections
tags.description:
A Document Section represents a polymorphic content block within a Document Document Sections are polymorphic content blocks that make up the structure of a Document. Each section has a resource_type which determines its content type: - Document::Text - Rich text content - Document::Heading - Heading with level (1-6) - Document::Gallery - Image gallery container - Document::Step - Procedural step with optional duration and gallery Sections maintain sort order within a document and can be rearranged. ATTRIBUTES FOR CONTENT-BASED SECTIONS (Text and Step): - content: Raw HTML content as stored in the database. For content containing inline images, the src attributes use relative paths in the format /organization_id/docs/document_id/developer/images/image_id. These relative paths are NOT S3 URLs - they must be parsed to extract the image metadata. Use this attribute when you need to preserve the original content for editing. - rendered-content: Processed HTML content with inline image paths converted to S3 URLs using the :original variant. This attribute is automatically generated and only included for Text and Step sections. Use this attribute for display/rendering purposes. The rendered-content attribute ensures that images are accessible with S3 URLs instead of relative web paths. CREATING SECTIONS WITH INLINE IMAGES: - Create an inline image (document image without gallery) using POST /api/document_images with target: { type: 'document', id: document_id } - Use the inline-resource-url value from the response in your section HTML - Create a Text or Step section with content: “

Text

” - The system will parse the paths and automatically convert them to S3 URLs in rendered-content IMPORTANT: Use the inline-resource-url format (the relative path), NOT the original-src S3 URL, when creating section content. The system needs to parse the relative path to extract organization_id, document_id, and image_id. Example: A Text section might have: ``` "content": "
Text with image
" "rendered-content": "
Text with image
" ``` IMAGE ATTRIBUTES (in document-images array): Document images (gallery and inline) include the following attributes: - name: The filename of the image - size: File size in bytes - document-id: If the image is used inline in a section (null for gallery-only images) - document-gallery-id: The gallery ID this image belongs to - target: Polymorphic target indicating where the image is used: { type: 'gallery'|'document', id: integer } - original-src: S3 URL for the full-resolution image (for display in galleries, etc.) - slim-src: S3 URL for the slim-sized variant (for display optimization) - thumbnail-src: S3 URL for the thumbnail-sized variant (for previews) - inline-resource-url: The relative path format for embedding in section content when CREATING sections. Format: /org_id/docs/doc_id/developer/images/image_id. Returns null for gallery images. This same attribute is used in the rendered-content as the reference path that gets converted to S3 URLs. The inline-resource-url is used for both: - CREATING/UPDATING sections with inline images (as the relative path) - Reference in rendered-content processing (parsed to extract IDs) The target attribute indicates the image's primary placement: - { type: 'gallery', id: N } - Image in a gallery container (inline-resource-url is null) - { type: 'document', id: N } - Image used inline in document section (inline-resource-url is the path) Note: Gallery images have document-gallery-id set but document-id may be null. Inline images have both document-id and document-gallery-id set if they are attached to a step's gallery.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description:
Document

The Documents resource allows you to manage documents on your account.

tags.name: Domains
tags.description:
A domain refers to a domain name, such as example.com.

The Domains resource allows you to retrieve information about all domains in your account.

A domain can belong to only one organization.

tags.name: Expirations
tags.description:
An expiration refers to a date associated with another resource's expiration

The Expirations resource allows you to view collected information about the expiration dates for your assets. To create, update or delete an expiration, a request must be made to the expiration's associated resource's endpoint.

A single expiration can belong to only one resource in one organization, but expirations can come from any organization.

tags.name: Exports
tags.description:
An export refers to a data export of either a single organization or current account.

This resource allows you to manage exports on your account.

An export can only belong to one account. Each export can have data for a single organization that belongs to current account or for all organizations of the current account.

tags.name: Flexible Asset Fields
tags.description:
A flexible asset field refers to a field in a flexible asset type.

This resource lets you manage all of the flexible asset fields in your account. The `name-key` attributes of fields can be used to POST new flexible assets.

Each flexible asset field has, at most, one immediate parent flexible asset type, and may be created after or at the same time as a new flexible asset type. Note: To avoid POST/PATCH errors, make sure that the name and order attributes are unique. In other words, no two fields with the same parent flexible asset type can have identical values for name or order. It's also required that at least one field has `show-in-list` set to true.

To explore the different fields that are available, refer to our [Flexible asset field definitions](https://help.itglue.kaseya.com/help/Content/2-using/flexible-assets/flexible-asset-field-definitions.html) article.

tags.name: Flexible Asset Types
tags.description:
A flexible asset type refers to a set of custom fields that can be used to generate structured documentation.

This resource lets you create and access information about the flexible asset types in your account. Flexible asset type IDs and flexible asset field `name-key` values can be used to POST new flexible assets.

The different flexible asset types let you document different parts of the IT infrastructure. For example, LAN is one flexible asset type, Backup is another, and Email yet another.

Note that when a flexible asset type is created with a flexible asset field, this creates a flexible asset field object. If the flexible asset field object is updated, this also updates the flexible asset type.

tags.name: Flexible Assets
tags.description:
A flexible asset refers to a record that has been created using a specific flexible asset type.

This resource lets you manage all of the flexible assets in your account.

Before you can have a flexible asset, a flexible asset type must exist. Flexible asset types pre-define the data structure as a table containing one or more fields with defined data types.

Every flexible asset (record) has a set of traits. Each trait is a JSON key-value pair. The key part of the key-value pair is the `name-key` for the corresponding flexible asset field. The value part is the field data. For example, if you have a key called `ip-address`, then you would enter an actual IP address as its value.

Note: The `use-for-title` property of fields in the flexible asset type is what determines the name of each associated flexible asset. If more than one field has the `use-for-title` property set to true, the text strings are joined into one string.

tags.name: Groups
tags.description:
A group is a collection of users.

The Groups resource allows you to retrieve information about groups.

tags.name: Locations
tags.description:
A location refers to a physical location and address where a client's users may work.

The Locations resource allows you to manage client location information in your account.

A location can belong to only one organization. Each configuration or contact can have one location, but it's not required.

tags.name: Logs
tags.description:
Log

This resource allows you to manage logs on your account.

tags.name: Manufacturers
tags.description:
A manufacturer refers to any computer product manufacturer.

This resource allows you to manage the manufacturer names for your account. Manufacturer IDs can be used to POST new configurations.

A manufacturer may be referenced by one or more configurations. Each configuration can specify one manufacturer name, but it's not required.

tags.name: Models
tags.description:
A model refers to a specific computer model, such as a Dell Latitude E7470.

The models resource allows you to manage the model names for your account. Model IDs can be used to POST new configurations.

A model name can belong to only one manufacturer and may be referenced by one or more configurations. Each configuration can specify one model name, but it's not required.

tags.name: Operating Systems
tags.description:
An operating system refers to any current or previous version of operating system software, for example, Windows 10.

The Operating Systems resource allows you to retrieve information about the operating systems that IT Glue supports. Operating system IDs can be used to POST new configurations.

Supported operating systems may be referenced by one or more configurations. Each configuration can have one operating system, but it's not required.

tags.name: Organization Statuses
tags.description:
An organization status refers to the status that can be maintained on an organization, for example, active or inactive.

This resource is used to manage information about organization statuses for your account. Organization status IDs can be used to POST new organizations.

An organization status may be referenced by one ore more organizations. Each organization can have one organization status, but it's not required.

tags.name: Organization Types
tags.description:
An organization type refers to the type categorization of an organization, for example, customer or vendor.

This resource is used to manage information about organization types for your account. Organization type IDs can be used to POST new organizations.

A organization type may be referenced by one or more organizations. Each organization can have one organization type, but it's not required.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description:
An organization refers to a client company.

The Organizations resource is used to manage information about organizations in your account.

Keep in mind that an organization can have one or more sub-organizations, but there is currently no support in the API for assigning a parent to create new sub-organizations. You would need to manually complete this task from your IT Glue account.

tags.name: Password Categories
tags.description:
A password category refers to the type categorization of a password.

This resource is used to manage information about your account's password types.

A password category may be referenced by one or more passwords. Each password can have one password category, but it's not required.

tags.name: Password Folders
tags.description:
Password Folder

This resource allows you to manage password folders on your account.

tags.name: Passwords
tags.description:
A password refers to a login credential for a managed system, application, or account.

This resource allows you to manage all passwords in your account.

For added security, accessing the actual password values is an optional setting that must be explicitly enabled for each API key. To enable this setting, select the “Password Access” checkbox under Account > Settings > API Keys. Once enabled, password values can be sent and received over HTTPS.

tags.name: Platforms
tags.description:
A platform refers to a type of operating system software, such as Windows or macOS, upon which applications or services are built.

The platform resource allows you to retrieve information about the platforms that IT Glue supports. Platform IDs can be used to POST new configurations.

Supported platforms may be referenced by one or more configurations. Each configuration can have one platform, but it's not required.

tags.name: Regions
tags.description:
A region refers to a subdivision of a country, such as a province, state, etc.

The Regions resource allows you to retrieve information about the region names that IT Glue supports. Region IDs can be used to POST new locations.

Supported regions may be referenced by one or more locations. Each location can have one region, but it's not required.

tags.name: Related Items
tags.description:
A related item refers to a link between two items.

Use the Related Items resource to manage related items in your account. For documentation on how to use a flexible asset's Tag field to create related items, refer to the Flexible Assets resource instead.

Note that related items (including those created from a Tag field) are accessed from the relevant endpoints (GET /configurations, GET /passwords, etc.) using the `include=related_items` parameter to return the related items in the relationships attributes of the requested objects.

Example: /configurations/1?include=related_items

tags.name: Resource Accesses
tags.description:
A resource access specifies which users/groups have access to the resource. Administrators have global access to resources in their IT Glue account

Resource Accesses allow you to manage resource accessibility on either the user or group level.

If a resource is restricted, user_resource_accesses represents a whitelist of users who can access the resource, and group_resource_accesses represents a whitelist of groups whose members can access the resource.

tags.name: User Metrics
tags.description:
A user metric refers to a raw metric used to calculate the reputation score of a user.

The User Metrics resource allows you to retrieve information about user metrics. These metrics are used by the engagement feature to calculate reputation scores.

A user metric covers all create, read, update, destroy (CRUD) activity done by a specified user, broken down by resource type.

UTC dates and date filters are available to allow metrics to be broken down into specific time periods up to one week and then offset to local time.

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
A user refers to anyone who can authenticate to IT Glue.

This resource allows you to retrieve information about the users in your account.

**Reputation** **Scores**

The returned data for each user will include their reputation score from the engagement feature in IT Glue. This score reflects all actions taken in the account for as long as the account has existed. The following point system is used:

- Created - 10 points
- Updated - 5 points
- Viewed - 1 points

The raw user metrics used to calculate scores are continually tracked for each user and reputation scores updated on an hourly basis. These raw metrics are part of a separate User Metrics resource.

get.summary: List all documents for a particular organization.
get.description:
Returns a list of documents for a specified organization.

Sub-documents (documents created inside another document) have no folder of their own: they belong to the folder of their parent. Each document has a document-id attribute: null for a top-level document, or the id of the parent document for a sub-document.

Sub-documents in the list:

```
Root list (filter[document_folder_id] omitted or 0)  — top-level documents only
filter[document_folder_id]=<id> (or a list of ids)   — documents in the folder(s) and their sub-documents
filter[document_folder_id]=null                      — all documents, sub-documents included
```

Filtering by document_id:

```
Omit filter[document_id]       — the defaults above
filter[document_id]=null       — top-level documents only (also 0); excludes sub-documents in folders too
filter[document_id]=<id>       — only the sub-documents of that document. filter[document_folder_id]
                                 is ignored, because sub-documents have no folder of their own.
```

Filtering by document_folder_id:

```
Omit filter[document_folder_id]        — returns only root-level documents
filter[document_folder_id]=null        — returns all documents (no filter applied)
filter[document_folder_id]=0           — returns only root-level documents
filter[document_folder_id]=<id>        — returns documents inside the specified folder
filter[document_folder_id]=1,2,3       — returns documents in folders 1, 2, or 3
filter[document_folder_id]=0,1,2       — returns root-level documents plus documents in folders 1 and 2
filter[document_folder_id]=null,1,2    — returns documents in folders 1 and 2 (null tokens are stripped in comma-separated context)
```

Note: Omitting the filter and passing [filter](document_folder_id)=null have different effects (root-level only vs. all documents). This asymmetry is intentional and kept for backward compatibility with the previous API default behavior.

Filtering by archived:

```
Omit filter[archived]        — returns archived and non-archived documents
filter[archived]=false       — returns only non-archived documents
filter[archived]=true        — returns only archived documents
```

Can be combined with [filter](document_folder_id).

get.summary: List all password folders for a particular organization.
get.description:
Returns a list of password folders for a specified organization.

Filtering by parent_id:

```
Omit filter[parent_id]        — returns all password folders
filter[parent_id]=null        — returns all password folders (no filter applied)
filter[parent_id]=0           — returns only root-level folders
filter[parent_id]=<id>        — returns direct child folders of the given parent folder
```

Note: Only a single value is accepted; comma-separated values are ignored and return empty results

Password counts:

```
passwords-count        — non-archived passwords directly in the folder
total-passwords-count  — non-archived passwords in the folder and all of its subfolders that the
                         requesting user can see, the number shown in the web Passwords list.
                         Only returned when with_total_passwords_count=true is passed.
```

Like the web, total-passwords-count only counts the passwords the passwords endpoint lists for the requesting user: deleted passwords, restricted passwords the user has no access to and other users' personal passwords are not counted, and neither are passwords in folders the user can't see. passwords-count does not check permissions and includes deleted passwords, so for a folder without subfolders it can be higher than total-passwords-count.
